result.title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
result.summary: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 R²Orch 递归自博弈编排范式：内循环自博弈在自选任务上改进 orchestrator，外循环改进内循环本身，并设计 Recursive Learnability 目标与 Skill Withdrawal 机制，在十二个数据集上验证其优于基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「撤除技能后表现不变即判定冗余」的贡献评估、以及失败蒸馏为技能再回灌参数的监督回路，可能为判断 latent 视觉内容是否被真正使用、诊断视觉旁路与信息坍缩提供可核查的借鉴线索。
